question.worked_solution:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

$$
{a}^{2}+2ab+{b}^{2}=(a+b)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
9{p}^{2}+30p+25.
$$

First, we write both the quadratic term and the constant term as perfect squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3p)^{2}+30p+(5)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3p)^{2}+2(15p)+(5)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the middle parentheses $(15p)$ as a product of $3p$ and $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(3p)^{2}+2(3p\cdot 5)+(5)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of a sum formula with $a=3p$ and $b=5.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}(3p+5)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
